rules: Answered right: exact match after lowercasing and removing punctuation and a, an, the; otherwise a fresh Claude Haiku answer judge (prompt below) for every answer that is not an abstention; nothing reused from earlier runs. Gold facts found: Claude Haiku splits each question's gold sentences into facts once (claims prompt), frozen and shared by every method and repeat (1,233 questions, 22,109 facts; one Natural Questions paragraph returned as several lists is joined into one list). An earlier count said 22,190, which does not reproduce; see DECISIONS 35. Then Claude Haiku marks each fact stated, contradicted or missing with a quote; a fact counts as found only when it is stated and code finds the quote word for word in the retrieved text. The judge sees the text given to the answer model, items de-duplicated and shuffled, never the method; tasks are shuffled across methods. Identical retrieved text (checked by hash) is judged once. The 400 MultiHop-RAG retrievals reused from 2 Nov were judged again. One Haiku subagent per file; a file failing the format check is re-run once by a fresh subagent; no verdict is edited by hand.
prompts: CLAUDE HAIKU GOLD-FACT JUDGE, STEP 1 (claims): the guide in every claims file, prompt version 2026-11-10.haiku.2

You split gold evidence sentences into the separate facts each one states.

For every item in this file, split each numbered sentence into facts. Cover
every fact in the sentence: do not drop names, numbers, dates, places, or
qualifiers such as 'former', 'first', or 'only'. Each fact is one short
self-contained statement in plain words that names its subject instead of
using a pronoun. Do not add anything the sentence does not say.

Write the verdict file named in your task as a JSON array with one object per
item, in any order:
{"id": "<item id>", "sentences": [["fact", "fact"], ["fact"]]}
The outer list has one entry per sentence, in sentence order (sentence 0 first).
Use only ids from this file and do not skip any item or sentence.
STEP 2 (judge): the guide at the top of every judge file

You check whether retrieved text states the facts of gold evidence sentences.

Use only the retrieved items. Do not use outside knowledge and do not reason
your way to a fact the text does not state; plain rewording, synonyms,
abbreviations and different formatting are fine.

For every fact give one status:
- stated: some item says it, with every specific matching (names, numbers,
  dates, places, who did what, qualifiers).
- contradicted: some item gives a different value for the same specific, such
  as another year or another person.
- missing: neither of the above.
If one item states the fact and another contradicts it, the status is contradicted.

Evidence for stated or contradicted facts: copy one continuous passage from
one item, character for character, with no ellipses or edits, and give that
item's number. Never join separate words into a quote that does not appear as
written; if the words are apart, quote the longer continuous passage that
contains them. A fact spread across items may take several quotes. The quotes
together must contain the words that state every specific of the fact (who,
what, numbers, dates, reasons); a quote that only sets the topic, or stops
before the specific, is not evidence. Missing facts take no evidence. Every quote is checked against the item text by a
program, and a quote that does not appear there counts as missing.

Write the verdict file named in your task as a JSON array with one object per
item, in any order:
{"id": "<item id>", "facts": [{"fact": "S.F", "status": "stated", "evidence": [{"item": 3, "quote": "..."}]}, ...]}
where "S.F" is the fact's label as given (sentence number, fact number).
Give exactly one entry for every fact label of the item. Use only ids from
this file and do not skip any item.
CLAUDE HAIKU ANSWER JUDGE: the guide in every answers file

You are grading a question-answering benchmark. Judge each item on its own.

For an "answer" item: is the model answer the same answer as any gold answer?
Count it correct when it names the same entity, value or yes/no decision, even
with different wording, extra title words, or a short explanation. Count it
wrong when it is a different entity, hedges between options, says it cannot
answer, or adds a claim that contradicts the gold answer.

For an "evidence" item: list the indexes of the gold sentences whose fact is
stated by the evidence text. A fact is stated when a reader of the evidence
alone would learn it (same entity, same claim, same date or number when the
sentence has one). Be strict: topic overlap or a generic description of the
same subject is not enough. Return an empty list when none.

Write verdicts.json as a JSON array with one object per item, in any order:
{"id": "...", "correct": true}             for answer items
{"id": "...", "supported": [0, 2]}          for evidence items
Use only ids from items.json and do not skip any item.

audit.disagreements_note: 4 of 200, all one way: Haiku found nothing, Opus found the fact (Haiku is the stricter judge, so gold-fact counts are if anything low). (1) HotpotQA Normal RAG, 'Chowder was created by C. H. Greenblatt': both said stated with the same quote; Haiku cited item 10, the sentence is in item 7, so the code check rejected it. (2) NQ Normal RAG, 'Can't Get You Out of My Head is recorded by Australian singer Kylie Minogue': Opus quoted 'It also topped the charts of Minogue's native country Australia'. (3) NQ RAPTOR, 'Washington's drinking age was 21 from after Prohibition onward': Opus quoted a table row 'Washington Age of majority since 1877 21 21 21 21'. (4) NQ HippoRAG, 'Eaton sets a test lap': Opus quoted a lap from a different episode and itself called the call borderline. The scoring rule was left unchanged.
